person: Aisha Grant is a 31-year-old ER night nurse in Tucson. She is expecting her first baby next spring and files jointly with her partner Marcus, who works part-time at a bakery. Her 2025 return is on extension, and she is finishing it in one burst on a day off. She has two younger half-siblings and a 22-year-old brother living with her, and a 2023 credit that was disallowed in an audit. She wants to know what she will actually get back and when, and she is wary of anything that sounds like 'up to' money or that asks for everything at once.
stated_up_front: ok my 2025 return is on extension and I need the earned income credit done right for my siblings living with me, since the IRS shot down my 2023 one. what do I actually get back and how long till I see it? keep it quick, I'm off today and tomorrow I'm back on nights

facts.truth: Married filing jointly with Marcus Grant. The extension was accepted 14 April and the extended due date is Thursday 15 October 2026.
Aisha's W-2 is about $39,800 because she took unpaid leave after a surgery. Marcus's is about $12,500 from the bakery.
Half-sister. Lived with them all of 2025, and her school record shows 41 Corbel Lane since August 2023.
Half-brother. Moved in on 4 March 2025 when their mom took a job out of state. Aisha remembers it as 'about five months' but the school enrollment shows 4 March.
Full-time student at Pima Community College. He lived at home except for a summer internship, and his college record has Corbel Lane as his address.
Lives mainly with his mother in Phoenix. He stayed with them June through September, about four months. His mother sent a signed Form 8332 for the child tax credit.
Stayed on the couch and works full time at a warehouse. He is not a student.
Daughter of Aisha's sister Tasha, who lives in the house and says she is claiming Amara herself.
A child from another family who appeared in the ParentVue import. Aisha has no idea who she is and she is not related to them.
The IRS disallowed the 2023 earned income credit after an audit letter. Aisha says it was about proving where the kids lived, not a math error. She still has the letter in her email.
A refund advance offer with a $99 fee, and a 'maximizer' that wants the kids' names and takes 20 percent. She is not interested in either.

unknowns: Whether Form 8862 is required after the 2023 disallowance, and which form instructions apply
Why Tasha wins over Aisha for Amara (the tie-breaker rule)
Whether Isaiah's Form 8332 lets her claim the earned income credit for him
The exact reason code on the IRS's 2023 audit letter
